assumptions.contact_use: every qualifying recorded pair-bin permits a hypothetical transfer in either direction under the selected bin rule
assumptions.nonstrict: multiple contact hops may occur in one bin; contact-bin endpoints are nondecreasing
assumptions.pair_filter: a pair qualifies using its total bin count over the whole window; retain all its in-window records, including earlier bins
assumptions.source_initialization: each source analyzed separately with a hypothetical signal available at window start
assumptions.strict: at most one contact hop per bin; successive contact-bin endpoints strictly increase
assumptions.waiting: unlimited lossless waiting within the window, including periods without records

limits: The strict/nonstrict/static inclusion compares models on the selected records; it is not a statistical or physical bound on real transmission.
Equal calendar windows and waiting edges do not establish equal attendance, device exposure, presence or retention of information.
Missing recorded contacts are not confirmed noncontacts; omitted real contacts and unknown transfer delays lie outside these models.
The archive actor universe and whole-window multi-bin filter use later records; this is not a past-only forecast or online decision rule.
Bin-endpoint arrival labels do not identify exact within-bin ordering or continuous transfer latency; BFS edge counts are not elapsed seconds.
Arrival summary comparisons condition on each graph's reachable ordered pairs, which need not be the same pairs across windows.
Actor-level temporal reachability is generally asymmetric and nontransitive; no static SCC, community or key-group metric is reinterpreted as temporal here.
This source contains no observed message deliveries, language labels, conflict measurements or activity attendance incidences.

measurement.arrival_unit: earliest reachable bin endpoint minus window start, including initial waiting; not a measured continuous transfer latency
measurement.conditional_arrival_statistics: summaries use reachable nonself ordered pairs; reachable pair sets can differ across windows and conventions
measurement.node_universe: all endpoint IDs anywhere in the reviewed archive, retained in every window
measurement.source_interval_definition: each endpoint t labels the recorded bin [t-20,t]
measurement.static_comparator: same-window same-threshold recorded-pair graph; unordered reachable counts are doubled for ordered-pair comparison

qualification.scope: retrospective paths on the reviewed recorded-bin graphs under declared conventions

research_question: How much static ordered-pair reachability remains when contact-bin order is respected, under strict and same-bin relay conventions?

scope.basis: paths through qualifying recorded 20-second contact bins
scope.deadline_fraction_denominator: all fixed ordered nonself actor pairs, including unreachable pairs
scope.hash_scheme: sha256 of compact UTF-8 JSON; sorted actor list, sorted (source,target) pairs, or sorted (source,target,absolute_bin_endpoint) triples
scope.nonstrict_rule: multiple contact hops with equal bin endpoints are allowed
scope.pair_qualification: retrospective full-window cumulative bin count; retain every qualifying pair's bin, including early bins
scope.signal_assumption: each source separately holds a hypothetical signal at the window start
scope.strict_rule: at most one contact hop in each recorded bin
scope.time_statistic: earliest reachable recorded bin endpoint minus window start; conditional on reachable ordered nonself pairs
scope.waiting_assumption: unlimited waiting within this window; retention is a model rule, not observed carrying
